title: The Oath of the Glass Steppe
premise: Wren Okonkwo, the last swordspeaker sworn to silence, keeps the ledgers of the Glass Steppe Guild, which trades in impossible things while pretending to be a mere counting house. When a child named Sef arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language that once commanded blades and started the Sundering War—Wren must choose between the oath that erased their name and the family forming around them. As guild rivals and war-hungry survivors of the old orders close in, Wren teaches Sef to speak safely, discovering that oaths can be rewritten rather than broken. In the end, Wren publicly unbinds their own oath to shield Sef, sacrificing their guild standing but gaining a true name, a found family, and a fragile peace bought at the cost of everything they were.
about_author: C. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from defunct merchant guilds before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people whose quiet competence hides extraordinary burdens.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren catalogs a week's impossible trades—bottled thunder, a debt paid in years—while maintaining the anonymity their oath demands. A storm brings a mud-caked child to the guild door, speaking words that make Wren's dormant blade hum on its wall peg. The emotional beat is wary recognition: Wren hears the First Tongue for the first time since their order was destroyed, and realizes invisibility has just ended.

chapters.title: What the Child Carried
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, with an interlude from guildmaster Odile. Hiding Sef among the clerks, Wren learns the child fled hunters wearing the sigil of the Ashen Compact, survivors of the old enemy. Odile suspects something and offers shelter at a price: the truth. The beat is found-family tenderness blooming under surveillance, as Wren breaks small rules—extra rations, a borrowed coat—and feels the oath tighten like wire.

chapters.title: The Price of the Oath
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The Compact breaches the Steppe, demanding the child; Odile, cornered, considers trading Sef to save the guild. Wren discovers the truth of their own oath—it was sworn not to protect secrets but to bury a massacre they witnessed as a child. Climax builds as Wren chooses: they draw their humming blade, speak the First Tongue aloud, and shatter decades of silence to buy Sef time to run.

chapters.title: A Name Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, closing with Sef. Standing before Compact leaders and the guild alike, Wren renounces the old oath and swears a new one—to Sef, freely given, witnessed by Odile and the assembled clerks. The Compact withdraws, unwilling to fight a swordspeaker reborn. The resolution lands on quiet cost and quiet gain: Wren loses rank and ledger, gains a name spoken aloud, and walks into the steppe dawn with family beside them.
